subject: Hosted API: sudden p95/p99 latency regression - queue accumulation
messages:

Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: high checkout latency - hosted API

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing a large jump in p95/p99 on your Hosted API around 08:50 PST this morning. Checkout calls for a small subset of customers (region: us-west) are spiking — p95 from ~120ms to ~1.8s and p99 up to ~3.2s. Error rate is still low (~0.7%) but throughput is delayed and user sessions are timing out.

Sample request id: req12345
Affected endpoint: POST /v1/generate (model: redwood-13b-instruct)

Attached is a quick chart of p95 trends from 07:30-09:10 and one sample request payload.

We’re on-hold for a marketing push at 10:00 and need this stabilized. Can your team confirm impact and ETA?

Thanks,
Luke

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:27:35 -08:00
Subject: RE: high checkout latency - hosted API

Team — quick triage notes (logs attached):

Observations:
- Around 08:45 we deployed a change to the batching controller that increased the batching window from 5ms to 20ms to optimize throughput for long-sequence workloads.
- After the change we see queue depth steadily rising on the request router for the redwood-13b-instruct family, particularly for short requests which do not benefit from larger batching windows.
- KV cache hit-rate unchanged; CPU/GPU utilization is within expected range. The backlog is on the request queue layer — requests waiting for batch formation. That matches the p95/p99 uplift with low error rate.

Attached: queue-metrics-2h.csv (request queue depth, batch sizes, latency percentiles)

Proposed immediate mitigation (can be done in <10m):
1) Roll the batching window back to 5ms for the redwood-13b-instruct model family.
2) Enable aggressive flush-on-threshold for short requests (flush at 4 requests or 6ms).
3) Temporarily increase worker pool target by +20% to absorb backlog while rollback propagates.

If the rollback is not acceptable for traffic pattern reasons, we can apply a targeted routing rule: short requests -> lower-batching variant.

I’ll stand by to execute — need ops approval to scale workers.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Serving Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: queue-metrics-2h.csv]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:34:10 -08:00
Subject: RE: high checkout latency - hosted API

Marissa — agreed with your analysis. Quick runbook steps I will apply now:

- Command: set-batching-config --model redwood-13b-instruct --window-ms 5 --flush-threshold 4  (will push to canary pools first)
- Command: autoscale set --pool hosted-us-west-infer --target-workers +20% --ttl 5m
- Monitor: p95/p99 across the router and model queues; rollback if we see regression in throughput for long sequence workloads.

Risks: small increase in per-token overhead for long sequences. I’ll validate cost delta post-fix.

Executing now and will post logs.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff SWE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Luke Turner <luke@finapps.com>, Ava Lin <ava.lin@finapps.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:46:02 -08:00
Subject: Update: Hosted API latency incident & next steps

Hi Luke / Ava — quick update from our ops team:

1) Root cause: an intentional increase to the batching window earlier this morning caused batch formation delays for short/low-token requests, leading to queue accumulation and elevated p95/p99.
2) Action taken: we've rolled batching window back to 5ms for the impacted model family and increased worker pool temporarily. Karthik applied the change and is monitoring.
3) Expected recovery: p95 should start trending back toward baseline within 5–10 minutes; p99 within 15–20 minutes as backlog drains.

We’ve scheduled a 30-minute bridge at 10:05 PST in case you want to join (link: https://zoom.us/j/123456789). Please reply if you see anything else.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with a root-cause postmortem and a mitigation plan to prevent batching config from impacting short-request traffic in the future.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
